conviction_note: The Q3 (Jun-Aug) numbers are new but the company has already set the bar (Q3 TCE around $24.5k/day, 'improved performance'). What is new and moves the stock is the Q4 tanker outlook and whether 2026 guidance comes back. Chemical spot has been soft to flat since mid-June (ICIS) and Odfjell guided its own Q3 lower. SNI has fallen after 7 of its last 10 results releases, including both prior Q3 prints on a softer Q4 rate outlook, and it goes in +13.7% over 20 days on a sector re-rating. So the size is kept at the new-numbers base (abs 6.5) and the direction is only a mild negative lean (p_up 42), not a confident call.

Reinstating the 2026 guide is possible but unlikely (about 30%) with Hormuz still closed; if it comes back, the sign depends on where it lands against H1 EBITDA of $358m.

findings.finding: The Q3 print's Q4 tanker outlook is likely flat to softer. ICIS has chemical spot rates ex-US Gulf weakening from mid-June and flat through late September, and Odfjell guided its Jul-Sep result lower on 'strong competition and reduced global volumes'. SNI goes in +13.7% over 20 days (Odfjell +~18% since 1 Sep) on a sector re-rating, and it fell on both prior Q3 prints when management flagged softer Q4 rates.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2024 (2024-10-02, E24: 'Stolt-Nielsen venter lavere skipsrater i fjerde kvartal') -6.83%; Q3 2025 (2025-10-02, E24: 'Resultatfall for Stolt-Nielsen') -4.93%; Q4 2024 (2025-01-30, 'Stolt-Nielsen venter lavere skipsrater', better than expected) -4.79%; guidance withdrawal 2026-04-09 -4.17%. Negative on 7 of the last 10 results days.
findings.original_quote: Vi utnyttet det sterke spotmarkedet i andre kvartal, mens sterk konkurranse og reduserte globale volumer per nå fører til et mer krevende marked. Etter et sterkt andre kvartal forventer vi at det underliggende nettoresultatet i 3Q26 blir lavere og nærmere nivået rapportert i 1Q26 (We captured the strong spot market in Q2, while strong competition and reduced global volumes are currently making for a more demanding market. After a strong second quarter we expect the underlying net result in 3Q26 to be lower and closer to the level reported in 1Q26.)
findings.why_not_priced: If the market had priced a softer Q4 for chemical tankers, SNI and Odfjell would not have re-rated +14-18% in September on flat chemical spot. The rally reads as pricing Hormuz restocking and swing-tonnage support for 2027. Stolt's own Q4 comment has not been made yet ('For Q4, it just unfortunately becomes too foggy'), and at 5-7 analysts on about $1.1m a day nobody has published a Q4 rate call I could find. The short register is empty, so the negative is not already carried by informed sellers.

baseline_tension: The finding agrees in sign with the priced lean (-0.685, which is the run-up with no short anchor) and argues against the +13.7% 20d / +22.9% 60d run-up continuing through the print. The run-up is sector-wide rather than SNI-specific, which is why p_up sits at 42 and not lower.
language_note: The NewsWeb filings were bilingual or English-only. Odfjell's Norwegian and English Q2 releases carry the same Q3 guide, so the primary documents added nothing new in Norwegian.

E24's Norwegian headlines on the last two Q3 prints ('venter lavere skipsrater i fjerde kvartal' 2024-10-02; 'Resultatfall' 2025-10-02) tie the post-Q3 selloffs to the Q4 rate comment. The English wires reported the numbers but not that framing.
